learning: Iteration 5 removed line loss on the oval but not on the curves, which fits footprint gaps at 20 mm spacing. If line loss is removed and the robot still leaves the track near 0.06 m, the next levers are wheel_track (yaw authority) and wheel_radius (speed), not more sensor changes.
notes: Tests whether the 16 mm footprint closes the residual line loss on the s-bend and slalom. Only sensor_size changes from iteration 5; the controller is unchanged.
rationale: Evidence: iteration 5 (seven sensors at 20 mm spacing, span ±0.06 m, lead 0.07 m, 12 mm footprints) removed line loss on the oval (0 events, progress 0.175, the best oval result so far). The s-bend and slalom still show 1 line-loss event per run, with max_error about 0.062 m and progress 0.165 and 0.110. Iteration 4 showed that lead and span are no longer moving the s-bend, and iteration 5's span change did not fix the curves. The Builder's hypothesis is that gaps between 12 mm footprints at 20 mm spacing let a 25 mm tape edge fall between sensors. I accept that test: sensor_size goes from 0.012 to 0.016 m, the largest allowed footprint, so each footprint overlaps its neighbours. Everything else stays fixed (seven sensors, y = 0.07 m, ±0.06 m span, track 0.10 m, mass 0.6 kg, wheel radius 0.03 m, body 0.18 x 0.12 m). Controller: iteration 5's weights are kept at about 33 times x, since the footprint change alters readings but not the lateral geometry. kp 1.25, kd 0.25, ki 0, base_speed 1.5 and last_direction also stay unchanged, so any change in result is attributable to the footprint. Expected: line_loss_events near 0 on the s-bend and slalom, max_error at or below about 0.06 m, and more progress. Risk: a larger footprint averages more of the edge, which can soften the signal near centre and raise slalom oscillation. The observation request is kept so the race reports those metrics.
